title: Doc Moon's millionaire con pitch
summary: Moon opened with sacks of pennies, claimed to be a millionaire who loved humanity, and threw money into the crowd.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And the people would just stand around all day, dance or...?

No, no dancing. They watched the show. Doc just... This is the people that's gathering, we're in the back there, in back of the stage there, and after you got a fairly good crowd, Doc Moon says, "Okay, boys, let's start the show. Doctor Moon's Medicine Show is now in session" -- or whatever he had to say. And we'd come out there and play maybe "Sand" or one of them fast tunes, "The Sheik of Araby" or one... This guy had to be the greatest con man in this whole world, Barry.
Doctor Moon.

Doc Moon. His opening words was... He always had a pocket-full of dimes, pennies and nickels, and maybe one quarter in the bunch -- mostly all pennies. And he'd come out there with this sack, or maybe two or three sacks, and it was all full of money. And he'd set one down. He'd set it down there, then he'd take his hand and dig in one of them, pull out a handful of money. And he's showing
Darensbourg - 75

the crowd all these pennies, you know. Well, he says, "You know what this is? Maybe you people know what this is. This is solid money. I want to tell you right now, I'm a millionaire, and I love humanity."
And he was a millionaire, huh.
Oh yes, he was. His people was millionaires. His people owned big salt mines...
Well, why did he do this?

Just for the love of it. He wanted to be an actor. Well, if you listened to him... He always told me the same thing. He almost got me convinced, I guess. But after looking at all of that bad medicine that he put out, you know... But what really got the people was, "I love humanity." When he got through talking to these people, they were almost crying to start with. "I love you people, and I know you. I know some of you people are sick." And literally, guys would wheel the people up there on crutches and every other thing, and the people who was bandaged up and suffering... Doc Moon would say, "Now, if you people here think I'm trying to make money off of you, you poor suffering souls, I want you to leave this lot. Get off. I'll have some of my security men..." His security men!
Did he have any security men?
Darensbourg - 76

No! [LAUGHS] "I'll have them throw you off the lot." Scaring these people and every other thing, you know. And you could see these poor country people, [WHISPERING], "Listen to that," or "Be careful, Vern, or we'll get throwed off this lot."
They wanted to see the show, huh?

Oh yeah. "Oh, we're gonna see some show." "If you think I'm here to make money off of you, I want you to get off the lot. Because I'm a millionaire, and I don't need any money. If you think I need your money here, here's a hundred dollars." Then he threw...
He threw it out to the people?!
Oh, yes. And you never seen such scrambling in all your life.
Well, with all that was going on, how would they know how much was in that little handful?
Well, they didn't know! Nobody knew.
If you picked up a penny, you might have thought your father picked up a quarter or a dime.

You'd hear guys yell out, "I found something!" Once in a while we'd find a dime or a nickel. There were quite a few nickels. And that's the thing that got 'em. It was so... In the meantime, the boxes of medicine are stacked up on the back in cardboard boxes.
